extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians preparing submissions to the Journal of the London Mathematical Society (authors considering where and how to submit)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting research articles to the Journal of the London Mathematical Society, including scope, length, peer-review model, and open-access options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance / suitability of contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles published in the Journal of the London Mathematical Society represent a significant advance in mathematical knowledge, or are deemed to stimulate new interest and research activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit work that either makes a clear, substantial advance in its area of mathematics or that is likely to stimulate further interest and research; this is the core acceptability standard for publication in the Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The articles have a minimum length of 18 pages and no maximum length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should meet the minimum length threshold (≥18 pages). There is no stated upper limit, distinguishing the Journal from concise-article venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published in this journal are peer reviewed. Identity transparency: Single anonymised. Reviewer interacts with: Editor. Review information published: None.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect single-anonymised peer review in which reviewers' identities are hidden; reviewers communicate via the editor. No peer-review reports or reviewer identities are published alongside articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial triage / possible desk rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may reject papers without external review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before external refereeing, editors exercise discretion to desk-reject submissions that do not meet scope, significance, or other editorial standards; ensure your manuscript clearly demonstrates fit and significance to reduce risk of immediate rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate journal selection among LMS titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Relation to other LMS journals: The Bulletin publishes concise research articles (20 pages and below) and the Proceedings publishes articles of the highest quality and significance across a broad range of mathematics. The Journal shares an Editorial Board with the Bulletin; both employ the same high standard of peer review. The Transactions is fully open access and the Journal of Topology is subject-focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the most appropriate LMS journal: for concise results consider the Bulletin (≤20 pages); for very high-impact, general-interest work consider the Proceedings; for topology-focused work consider Journal of Topology; for OA requirements consider the Transactions or LMS open-access options. Use these comparisons to decide whether the Journal of the London Mathematical Society is the right venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access options and funder compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal of the London Mathematical Society is a hybrid open access journal. By default, articles in the journal will be published on a subscription basis and only be accessible to journal subscribers. The journal has options for gold and green open access publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must check any open access requirements from their institution or funder and identify an appropriate route (gold or green). If you cannot identify a compliant open-access route with this journal, contact the journal team before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural guidance after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is accepted for publication in the Journal of the London Mathematical Society, it will be sent to the publisher for typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted manuscripts enter the publisher production process (typesetting and related steps). Authors with questions about items under review or at various production stages are given contact addresses for LMS and Wiley teams; consult the journal's 'what happens after acceptance' information for details.
